title: Indigenous and Afro-Mexican Communities “Lead the Way” in Analysis for the General Law on Peoples, Sheinbaum Says
author: Emir Olivares and Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by[Emir
Olivares](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Emir%20Olivares) and [Alonso
Urrutia](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alonso%20Urrutia) originally
appeared in the [October 12, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/12/politica/comunidades-
indigenas-y-afromexicanas-llevan-la-mano-en-analisis-para-la-ley-general-de-
pueblos-dice-sheinbaum), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. Commemorating the Day of the Resistance of the Peoples,
President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo stated that Indigenous and Afro-Mexican
communities "lead the way" in the discussions to present the **general law for
those peoples** to the Congress of the Union.

"We had the idea that perhaps on October 12, today, it could be delivered to
Congress, but there are still issues that it is important to keep consulting
on. That is why you lead the way, you have the word, you have the decision,
and until you tell us 'it's ready,' well, then we will not present it to the
Congress of the Union."

In the Marian courtyards of the National Palace, the president held a
"circular dialogue" with representatives of various Indigenous and Afro-
Mexican communities to mark the date.

![President Claudia Sheinbaum listens to representatives of Indigenous and
Afro-Mexican communities](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/10/2026-10-12-indigenous-law-
consultation-02-dialogue.jpg)President Claudia Sheinbaum listens to
representatives of Indigenous and Afro-Mexican communities at the ceremony for
the Day of the Resistance of the Peoples. Photo: Presidencia

From there, she highlighted that beyond remembering it as Día de la Raza
(Columbus Day), which was a Eurocentric vision, the objective of the
governments of the Fourth Transformation is for it to be recognized as the
**Day of the Resistance of the Peoples**.

> October 12 is no longer Día de la Raza. (Since 2020) the Senate of the
> Republic recognizes it as the Day of the Pluricultural Nation; but we like
> to recognize it as the Day of the Resistance of the Indigenous and Afro-
> Mexican Peoples, because if it were not for that resistance, Mexico today
> would not be what it is.
>
> President Claudia Sheinbaum

The head of the Executive stated that with the Fourth Transformation that
recognition did not remain only in words, but that with the **constitutional
changes of 2024** those communities were recognized as subjects of rights,
which had not happened in the constitutions of 1824, 1857 or 1917.

"In the Constitution of 2024 it was established in the second article of the
Constitution that Indigenous and Afro-Mexican peoples are subjects of law and
of all rights. That is historic because it had never been recognized before.

"And when we arrived (at the Presidency), first (we proposed) that a general
law must be made, but if the second article of the Constitution recognizes
that there must be Indigenous consultation, there's no way the general law
can't emerge from the peoples and from the consultation!"

For that reason, the president stressed that they will wait for the voice of
the communities to take the law to Congress.
